result.topic_en: Spherical-trigonometry manipulations relating angles φ, a, b, e, h, δ, θ (sines, cosines, tangents), apparently deriving relations between sides and angles of a spherical triangle; part of the right side is written upside down.
result.transcription:
$\sin\delta = \frac{\sin\varphi \sin a}{\cos b}$
$\cos h \tang\varphi = \frac{\cos\delta \cos e \cos b}{\sin\varphi \sin a}$
$\cos a \sin b = \frac{\cos\varphi \sin h \sin e \cos h \sin\varphi \tg\varphi \sin a}{\cos e [-\cos b-]}$
$\cos b \sin b = \sin\varphi^2 \tg e \tang a \cos h \sin h$
$\sin a \cos b = \frac{\sin\varphi^2 \sin a}{\cos b} + \cos\varphi \cos\delta \cos h \cos e$
$\frac{\sin a}{\cos b}$ $[-+ \frac{\cos\varphi \cos h^2 \tg\varphi \sin\varphi \sin a}{\cos b}-]$ $\frac{\cos\varphi \cos\delta \tg\delta \cos e^2}{\tang\varphi}$
$[-+ \frac{\sin\varphi^2 \cos h^2 \sin a}{\cos b}-]$
$+ \frac{\cos\varphi^2 [-\sin\delta-]}{\sin\varphi} \frac{\cos e^2 \sin a}{\cos b}$
$- \frac{\cos\varphi^2 \sin a \cos e^2}{\cos b}$
$\sin b^2 = \cos\varphi^2 \sin e^2$
$\pm \sin b = \cos\varphi \sin\theta$
$1 = \frac{[-\sin\varphi \sin a-]}{\cos b \sin\delta}, = \frac{\tang\delta \cos e}{\cos h [-\tang\varphi-]}$
$= \frac{\cos\varphi \sin a \cos e}{\cos b \cos\delta \cos h}$
$\frac{\cos\varphi \sin a \cos e}{\cos b \cos\delta}$
(upside down:)
$\frac{\sin e}{\sin h} \cos a \cos b = \cos a \cos b [?] - \frac{\sin\varphi}{\sin\delta}$
$\frac{\sin e}{\sin h} \frac{\cos b \cos\delta}{\cos a \cos b} = \frac{\cos\delta \cos\varphi}{\cos a \cos b} - \frac{\sin\varphi \cos\delta}{\tg\delta}$ [?]
$\sin e (\cos h - 1) = \tg\delta \tg\varphi [?] - \frac{\cos\delta \cos\varphi}{\cos a \cos b} - \frac{\tang\delta}{\cos h \tang\varphi}$ [?]

methods.what: Relation for sin δ in terms of φ, a, b (spherical sine rule type)
Expression for cos h tan φ
Product relation for cos b sin b
methods.quote: $\cos b \sin b = \sin\varphi^2 \tg e \tang a \cos h \sin h$

methods.what: Decomposition of sin a cos b
methods.quote: $\sin a \cos b = \frac{\sin\varphi^2 \sin a}{\cos b} + \cos\varphi \cos\delta \cos h \cos e$

methods.what: Identity equating ratios to 1 by combining the previous formulas
